clue.text: Confirm am entering outer space, encapsulated

indicators.note: encapsulated says the answer sits sealed inside the run of clue words, as in a capsule

explanation.surface: Someone confirms they are boarding a rocket into outer space, sealed in a capsule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encapsulated' signals the letters held within 'Confirm am entering': drop CON and ERING from the ends.
explanation.definitionFit: The firmament is the vault of the heavens, the sky seen as an arch, so it serves for outer space.

clue.text: Predict the French will occupy this section of the ship

parts.note: to predict is to forecast
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone forecasts that the French will take over part of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will occupy' looks like a container signal, but the French article simply comes after the prediction; a forecastle is usually spelt and said fo'c'sle.
explanation.definitionFit: The forecastle (fo'c'sle) is the forward part of a ship's upper deck, where the crew traditionally lived.

clue.text: Discerning part of a fish skulking in water plant

indicators.note: something skulking in a place is lurking hidden inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass growing in water
a fin is part of a fish

explanation.surface: A fish hides among the reeds, only a part of it showing.
explanation.definitionFit: A refined palate is a discriminating one, so refined means having cultivated, discerning taste.

clue.text: Stadium where there's a near riot

indicators.note: a riot throws everything into disorder, so the letters of the two words are scrambled

explanation.surface: Trouble almost breaks out in the crowd at a sports stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riot' signals an anagram of A NEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed space for sport or spectacle, the Roman word for a stadium's floor of sand.

clue.text: Utterances of former newsman about Swiss town

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first pieces surround the town

parts.note: the press stands for journalists, the newsmen collectively
Sion is the capital of the Swiss canton of Valais

explanation.surface: A retired reporter is quoted talking about a small town in Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SION inside EXPRESS, between its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Expressions are phrases or sayings, things spoken, so they are utterances.

clue.text: Three-point endeavour, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: in rugby a try is the attempt that scores points

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a three-point effort counts as a score.
explanation.walkthrough: A try in rugby union was worth three points until 1971. TRI- is the prefix meaning three, as in tricycle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tri- is the combining form for three, as in triangle and tripod.

clue.text: Back copies one got in colour

indicators.note: one piece got into the other means it is placed inside
back says the word for copies is read in reverse

parts.note: to ape is to copy, so apes means copies
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Old back issues are reprinted with one in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns APES into SEPA, and 'got in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown tone, named for cuttlefish ink and seen in old photographs.

clue.text: Gypsum seen to be deposited in mineral spring, reaching river

parts.note: something deposited has been set down, so it sat
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: Mineral is seen settling in a spring before flowing on to a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen to be' and 'reaching' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin spar is a fibrous, silky variety of gypsum (also of calcite), so it is a kind of that mineral.

clue.text: Take the lead and get caught in deeper entanglement

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the jumbled letters
an entanglement is a tangle, so the letters of deeper are twisted into a new order

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone gets ahead in a race only to be snared deeper in a tangle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entanglement' signals an anagram of DEEPER (PREEDE), and 'in' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To precede is to go before, which is to lead the way.

clue.text: Found in church in a state of collapse

indicators.note: in a state of says the answer sits within the following word

explanation.surface: A church is discovered to be falling down.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: the answer is something found in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the vaulted semicircular recess at the east end of a church, behind the altar.

clue.text: Flier brought to grief by a gun

indicators.note: something brought to grief is wrecked, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An aviator is shot down by a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought to grief' signals an anagram of FLIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled firearm with a grooved bore, so it is a type of gun.

clue.text: To be blunt, a clue here could seem futile

explanation.surface: Speaking frankly, a clue placed here might look like a waste of time.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is literal: without a sharp end. The second is figurative: with no purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Blunt describes a tool with no sharp tip; futile describes an effort with no purpose or use.

clue.text: A novel scene, with two hundred injured now on the way to recovery

definitions.text: now on the way to recovery

indicators.note: injured means damaged, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two hundred is CC

explanation.surface: An unusual sight: two hundred casualties now getting better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' signals an anagram of A NOVEL SCENE plus CC.
explanation.definitionFit: Convalescence is the period of gradual recuperation after illness, the state of someone who is mending.

clue.text: Left lancers in a sorry condition

definitions.text: Left lancers in a sorry condition

indicators.note: in a sorry condition suggests a mess, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Cavalrymen left behind are in a wretched state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a sorry condition' signals an anagram of LEFT LANCERS. Read whole, a cavalry lancer's crest has fallen: he is dejected.
explanation.definitionFit: Crestfallen means dejected, downcast after a setback, as cavalry abandoned on the field would be.

clue.text: Low joint, technically speaking, where a star has a slug, being fuddled

indicators.note: being fuddled means confused or tipsy, so the letters are muddled up

explanation.surface: A celebrity takes a slug of drink and gets tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being fuddled' signals an anagram of A STAR plus A SLUG; 'slug' looks like the creature but is a gulp of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Astragalus is the anatomist's term for the talus, the ankle bone, low in the leg where it forms a joint.

clue.text: Sick at heart and head? It's due to gravity

parts.note: someone sick at heart is sad
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A person feels ill in heart and head, and blames it on gravity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gravity' suggests the physical force but means solemnity, a grave mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravity in the sense of solemnity or grave circumstances brings on unhappiness and sorrow.

clue.text: Compensation paid for poor motel menu

indicators.note: poor means badly made, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Guests demand a refund for a dreadful roadside motel's food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' signals an anagram of MOTEL MENU.
explanation.definitionFit: An emolument is a salary, fee or payment for work, which is compensation.

clue.text: A leading figure in society — newsmen follow me back

indicators.note: follow places the journalists after the first piece
back says the word me is read in reverse

parts.note: the press means journalists collectively

explanation.surface: A celebrity notices reporters tailing her home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the word me around, and 'follow' says the journalists come after it; 'leading figure' hints at a figurehead but means a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: An empress is a female ruler of an empire, which puts her at the top of society.

clue.text: Stagger on, with little work and nothing at the end of it? The river!

parts.note: to limp is to walk unevenly, to stagger
op is short for opus, a work, so it is a little work
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone struggles on with little work and nothing to show for it, then reaches the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the end of it' just places O last. The Limpopo is the river in southern Africa made famous by Kipling's Just So Stories.
explanation.definitionFit: The Limpopo is a major southern African river flowing to the Indian Ocean through Mozambique.

clue.text: Sums are wrong — rubber needed

indicators.note: wrong means incorrect, so the letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Arithmetic is off, so an eraser is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubber' seems to be the British word for an eraser, fitting the sums, but is one who rubs. 'wrong' signals an anagram of SUMS ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseur is a man who gives massages, kneading muscles, so he rubs people for a living.

clue.text: The short oarsman's a tosser

indicators.note: short says the word is cut off before its end

parts.note: an oarsman is a rower

explanation.surface: The little oarsman turns out to be a jerk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims The to TH. 'tosser' is British slang for an idiot, but here simply means one who tosses.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrower is one who hurls or flings things, so anyone who tosses something.

clue.text: Device to get fish out of the river

indicators.note: to get here means to take in, so the verb's letters hold the river

parts.note: to winkle out is to extract, to fish out

explanation.surface: Someone wants a gadget for pulling fish from the river.
explanation.walkthrough: A winkle is a sea snail, but here 'winkle' is the verb to prise out, with R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrinkle in the informal sense is a clever trick or dodge, a handy device or gimmick.

clue.text: Deep personal probing and louse, endless vigorous combing revealed

indicators.note: vigorous means energetic, so the trimmed letters are shaken up
endless says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: combing an area is searching it thoroughly

explanation.surface: A parent finds lice during a hard, thorough combing of a child's hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts LOUSE to LOUS, and 'vigorous' rearranges it into SOUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Soul-searching is close examination of one's own conscience and motives, an inner probing.

clue.text: Type of carp we hear lay filleted and, in this way, shrinking

indicators.note: we hear says the carp's name is spoken aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: the koi is an ornamental Japanese carp

indicators.note: a filleted fish has its middle removed, so only the first and last letters of lay remain

explanation.surface: A fish is cooked and served, and someone shyly hides from it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'shrinking in this way': an adverb, as the answer is.
explanation.definitionFit: To act coyly is to act shyly or bashfully, which is behaving in a shrinking manner.

clue.text: Parrots featuring in a piece of tapestry

indicators.note: featuring in a piece of says the answer is part of the following word

explanation.surface: Birds are pictured in a section of woven wall hanging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrots' looks like a noun but is a verb: imitates.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat mindlessly, and to ape is to mimic, so both mean copy.

clue.text: Bit by bit assembling baked food for church supper?

parts.note: a pie is a baked dish
CE is the Church of England
a supper is a meal

explanation.surface: A congregation gathers pies for a parish supper.
explanation.definitionFit: Piecemeal means done gradually in separate stages rather than all at once.

clue.text: Drop, in the ocean

parts.note: a fall in the sea's level, the outgoing of the tide, punning on a drop in the ocean

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'a drop in the ocean' means a trivial amount, but here the drop is a fall in the water level.
explanation.definitionFit: The ebb is the receding of the tide, when the sea falls away from the shore.

clue.text: Simple rustic coupling with first love

parts.note: a yoke couples two oxen together

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of love

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin is pairing up with his first sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: A yokel is an unsophisticated country person, a bumpkin.

clue.text: Fish for chap on a fat-free diet

explanation.surface: A man on a diet orders fish instead.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme, Jack Sprat could eat no fat, while his wife could eat no lean.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprat is a small sea fish of the herring family; Jack Sprat is the nursery-rhyme man who ate no fat.

clue.text: Complaint? Some riders are said to have bowed to supporters

definitions.text: Complaint? Some riders are said to have

parts.note: bandy means curved outward, bowed
legs are what hold us up, our supporters

explanation.surface: Horse riders are said to bow to their fans.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse riders are said to develop bowed legs from years in the saddle. 'bowed to' looks like a gesture of respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandy legs are legs curving outward at the knee, an ailment jokingly blamed on horse riding.
